reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it is framed as a tutorial and promotion for a survey-earning app, showing registration, survey interfaces, profile questions, and reward flows. Although it asks viewers to use a description link and mentions referral rewards, these are presented as walkthrough steps without evidence of impersonation, theft, or a false transaction outcome. A separate Telegram advertisement is also noted but is not established as the video's central solicitation.

citations.quote: Real Research | New Survey Earning App Of 2020 | Earn money by completing Surveys
I'm going to tell you about this survey where you simply have to complete some surveys and you have a lot. You'll get up to 80 rupees on your stay.
But if you invite one of your trends to succeed, you'll get up to 40 rupees.
You will get the link in the description. Simply click on that link and then place the torse. The direct download of the application is fine.
The verification code will verify both your email and mobile phone number after that. The registration is successful.

opening.argument: The video ties a promised monetary or token reward to a chain of viewer actions: completing surveys, registering through the description link, creating a wallet, and submitting account information. The offer is not merely informational. The title advertises earning money by completing surveys, while the walkthrough says viewers can receive up to 80 rupees and later identifies 10 TNC in the balance as worth up to 80 rupees. The registration screen itself pairs “Register and earn TNC” with email and password fields, and the survey flow offers a large token reward behind a “START SURVEY” action. That is a low-barrier acquisition pitch in which participation and account data are presented as the route to a reward.

citations.quote: You will get the link in the description. Simply click on that link and then place the torse. The direct download of the application is fine.
then you will see in the balance, you will have 10 TNCs, which means you have got up to 80 rupees.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this a tutorial does not remove the solicitation. The very walkthrough directs viewers to an external download and explains registration, wallet creation, and reward collection. The reference statement's acknowledgment that rewards are mentioned actually confirms the central promise-action relationship; it does not establish that the reward is reliable or that the requested account and wallet steps are harmless. Showing an interface demonstrates only that an app exists, not that the advertised earnings will be delivered.

citations.quote: If you create the wallet then you will have to enter your password
you will click on Collect Reward, so you will have the option to click Go to Wallet

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted instructions show an ordinary survey workflow, not a deceptive transaction. They do not show that anyone paid money, that a viewer was charged, or that the app falsely represented its identity. The registration screen merely requests ordinary account fields, and the survey screen displays an in-app reward; neither proves the reward is fraudulent. A promised reward linked to completing surveys can be a conventional promotion without becoming a scam.

citations.quote: I'm going to tell you about this survey where you simply have to complete some surveys and you have a lot. You'll get up to 80 rupees on your stay.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: unusually easy earnings, token-denominated rewards, extensive KYC-style questions, and wallet-related confirmation. The walkthrough presents up to 80 rupees for simple surveys, while another screen advertises “+ 180000 TNC” for a gambling-related survey. Progression also asks for relationship status, estimated annual revenue, and ownership of branded goods. After completing a survey, the user is told the reward will arrive after confirming a transaction on the wallet network and is offered “GO TO WALLET.” Even without proof of a completed loss, this combination makes the offer materially more concerning than an ordinary survey advertisement.

citations.quote: You'll get up to 80 rupees on your stay.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The reference framing isolates each screen as a benign interface and ignores their cumulative effect. A token reward, gambling-themed survey, personal financial profiling, and wallet-network confirmation are not necessary to prove a loss, but they are relevant warning signals in assessing whether an easy-income pitch is trustworthy. The fact that payment is not established is precisely why the promotional certainty should be treated cautiously, rather than accepted from the app's own screens.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals show unusual design choices, not deception. The screen says the reward follows confirmation on the wallet network, which is consistent with a token platform's stated process; it does not say users must deposit money. KYC questions can support audience profiling for surveys, and the quoted evidence does not establish that the displayed token amount has cash value or that any outcome was misrepresented. Suspicion cannot substitute for evidence of a scam.

opening.argument: Although presented as an informational walkthrough, the video functions as a recruitment and promotion channel. It directs viewers to use the description link, download the application, join a Telegram channel for updates, and invite another person for up to 40 rupees. The surrounding channel material also displays an advertisement promising 50% profit while urging viewers to invite friends. This is not detached reporting: the presentation supplies the route to participate and emphasizes rewards for bringing in additional users, making the apparent tutorial a solicitation for sign-ups and referrals.

citations.quote: But if you invite one of your trends to succeed, you'll get up to 40 rupees.
You will get the link in the description.
Don't Forget to join our Telegram Channel for Latest Earning App Updates.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The label “tutorial” does not describe the video's practical function. Viewers are told where to download the app, how to register, how to complete KYC, and how to claim rewards; those are participation instructions. The additional referral payment and Telegram direction reinforce audience acquisition. Even if the Telegram advertisement is not the main offer, the video's own referral instruction is enough to show promotional steering rather than neutral education.

citations.quote: Every survey you get, you get 50 to 100 pips

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A walkthrough can be promotional without being fraudulent. The video explains how a survey app works and discloses the referral reward rather than hiding it. A one-level invitation incentive does not establish a downline, tiered matrix, or deceptive recruitment scheme. The separate Telegram post cannot be treated as proof about the survey app, and the available material does not show that viewers were compelled to pay or that the advertised process failed.

citations.quote: But if you invite one of your trends to succeed, you'll get up to 40 rupees.
